newsitem.title: UK: New strike threat as builders balloted on strike.
newsitem.headline: New strike threat as builders balloted on strike.

text.p: Britain's trade unions raised the spectre of a new strike threat on Wednesday, with the announcement that 40,000 building workers are to be balloted on strike action next week.
The GMB and Transport and General Workers (T&G) unions will send out ballot papers next Wednesday -- the day British Airways Plc cabin crew are set to start a series of 72 hour strikes over pay.
The building strike ballot result is expected on August 25, with unions expressing confidence of clinching enough support to press ahead.
If the GMB and T&G receive backing from members, the unions said they plan to target some of the highest-profile construction projects in the country.
"We will be targeting sites like the Millennium project, the Jubilee Line (on the London Underground) and the second runway at Manchester airport," a GMB spokeswoman told Reuters.
She said the action would be taken against construction company employers who are members of the Construction Confederation -- the body which negotiates on pay for the industry.
"If the strike ballot is backed, all the big construction companies will be hit," said the GMB spokeswoman citing names like John Laing Plc, George Wimpey and Costain Group Plc.
The row flared up after the Confederation withdrew its annual pay offer without submitting a replacement -- creating an effective pay freeze for the coming year, said union officials.
"There is a feeling that the construction industry is now booming and that they can afford a pay rise," said the GMB official. The last time builders were balloted on strike action was in 1973.
